place: A porcelain plain of sclera cracked into slabs, where the zero-gauge capillaries run as crimson seams between them and each crossing is a vein bridge toward the wet pink caruncle in the eye's corner.

observations.what: Fine branching red capillaries crossing the left sclera
Moist pink caruncle with a white specular highlight at the inner corner
Pale buff sclera fog, smooth and hard like glaze

measured.role: Deep outer space void, central pupil, and deepest eyelid crease shadows
Soft shadow framing the eyeball and shading the socket
Dark teal-grey transitional tones between space and the eyelid rim
Midtone skin shading along the brow ridge and eyelid margins
Outer ring of the iris and shadowed face of the planetary ring
Pale highlight tone across the sclera and inner lower lid margin
Desaturated beige midtone bridging lid highlights to shadow
Warm brown-red vascular shading in the medial caruncle and crease

palette.notes: Porcelain ivory ground, crimson vein paths, blush pink raised slabs, clinical white stone; cliffs flushed rose over wine.

shape.summary: Two ivory porcelain posts wrapped in spiralling crimson vein bands, a crimson vein beam arched across the top.
An upright chunky wedge of ivory glaze with a crimson crack line up one face, leaning slightly.
A coral-like tangle of crimson beams branching upward from a dark red root block.
A red biconcave disc tipped on edge against a small ivory chock.
A white clinical post with a hooded head throwing a flat bar of cyan light.
A flat decal of branching thin crimson lines.

creatures.source: The medial caruncle with its wet highlight.

shape.summary: A knotted mound of stacked rose and coral blocks with crimson vein ribs running down its sides, holding a large glossy tear pearl of white and cyan with a bright highlight on top.

creatures.pose: caruncle: a knotted pink flesh mound holding up a large glossy tear pearl, veins running from its base into the plain.
creatures.why: ANALYSIS.medium.marks and the painting's inner corner: the one wet, living spot on the sclera plain.

legend.R: raised ground (plateau, one or more blocks above G)

focal.what: A knotted mound of stacked rose and coral blocks with crimson vein ribs running down its sides, holding a large glossy tear pearl of white and cyan with a bright highlight on top.

composition.mass: Slabs scattered across the plain, the tallest in the back-left corner.
composition.read: A cracked porcelain plain crossed along its veins to the caruncle.

lighting.notes: The capillaries are fine detail the painter drew with a zero-gauge brush (ANALYSIS.medium.marks); even, bright light lets each one read.

rules: Vein path crosses every crack at its bridge.
Shards stand on slab edges, never on the vein path.

lens.aspect: ANALYSIS.medium.marks: delicate branching red capillaries in fluid crimson ink across the buff sclera, and the moist medial caruncle in the inner corner
lens.place: A porcelain plain of sclera cracked into slabs, where the zero-gauge capillaries run as crimson seams between them and each crossing is a vein bridge toward the wet pink caruncle in the eye's corner.
lens.summary: Ivory slabs split by void cracks, crimson vein paths branching across them, standing porcelain shards and vein knots, slit lamps beside the path, and a glossy tear pearl on a pink caruncle knot at the far slab.
lens.differs: The earlier readings kept capillaries as tiny decals at the edge; here they organise the whole map, and the focal figure is the caruncle and its tear, not the pupil.

shaper.name: shards
shaper.why: Glaze crazing splits the sclera into plates; the shards shaper cuts slabs apart with void seams and one crossing each, which become the vein bridges.

surface_mix.why: Mostly bare porcelain, blush where the sclera warms toward the lids, a few white glaze highlights.

cliff_treatment.why: The crack edges show the flesh under the glaze: pink over deep red.

lighting.why: The capillaries are fine detail the painter drew with a zero-gauge brush (ANALYSIS.medium.marks); even, bright light lets each one read.

figure_pose.why: ANALYSIS.medium.marks and the painting's inner corner: the one wet, living spot on the sclera plain.

approach.from: the far slab at the camera-right corner
approach.shape: Follow the crimson vein from slab to slab over the crack bridges, branching dead ends peeling off, to the caruncle on the tallest slab.

threshold.kind: A porcelain arch bound in veins at the last crack.
